subsystems.name: High-resolution spectrograph
subsystems.role: spreads starlight finely enough to resolve narrow absorption lines from gas boiling off a comet.

subsystems.name: Wavelength calibration and drift control
subsystems.role: keeps the wavelength scale steady to metres per second so a faint absorption feature is not confused with instrument drift.
parts: laser frequency comb or thorium–argon lamp

subsystems.name: Telescope and fibre feed
subsystems.role: collects enough photons to measure a transit lasting only hours; a stable fibre scrambles the beam to the spectrograph.

subsystems.name: Simultaneous photometric channel
subsystems.role: measures the broadband dimming that accompanies the gas, separating dust from pure gas release.
parts: space photometer or fast-frame CCD camera

subsystems.name: Observing scheduler
subsystems.role: because the events are unpredictable, the system needs high cadence, long baselines and target-of-opportunity triggers.

subsystems.name: Modelling and reduction pipeline
subsystems.role: turns a shifting line profile into orbital and outgassing parameters.

subsystems.name: Archive and follow-up network
subsystems.role: stores every spectrum so rare events can be correlated with other observatories later.

buildSteps.title: Select host stars
buildSteps.detail: Pick nearby, young stars with known debris disks and gas — systems where planet formation may still be delivering volatiles inward.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the spectrograph
buildSteps.detail: Grind and align the echelle optics, then seal them in a vacuum tank on a vibration-isolated bench so the dispersion stays fixed over months.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Fit a laser frequency comb or reference lamp and a second fibre so every exposure is calibrated simultaneously with the science light.

buildSteps.title: Couple the telescope
buildSteps.detail: Run a fibre from the telescope focus to the spectrograph, with an image slicer and a guider that holds the star on the fibre as the atmosphere wobbles.

buildSteps.title: Add the photometric channel
buildSteps.detail: Either negotiate observing time on a space photometer or install a fast-readout camera that can stare at the star with sub-minute cadence.

buildSteps.title: Plan the campaign
buildSteps.detail: Write a cadence scheme that samples nights repeatedly over seasons; the events are aperiodic, so only long coverage catches them.

buildSteps.title: Reduce and detect
buildSteps.detail: Subtract a stellar template, cross-correlate each exposure, and flag narrow absorption that appears redshifted relative to the star's lines.

buildSteps.title: Model and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Fit the absorption profile and the photometric dip together to get gas velocity, column density, gas-to-dust ratio and a rough orbit for the evaporating body.

buildSteps.title: Archive and compare
buildSteps.detail: Publish spectra so the same star can be re-examined when independent data, such as space photometry, later becomes available.

prerequisites.why: the calcium lines tracing exocomet gas are narrow and faint, so resolving power and wavelength stability set the detection limit.
uninterrupted, precise brightness monitoring catches the dimming from dust and puts a cadence floor under the ground-based spectra.
a transit signal of a few metres per second cannot be separated from instrumental drift without it.
translating a line profile into a volatile delivery rate still relies on simplified physics.
monitoring programmes conflict with the short, competitive observing blocks most telescopes favour.

pathway.milestone: dedicated spectrograph monitoring of nearby young stars, with Beta Pictoris as the archetype, running since the 1980s
pathway.unlocks: the first measurements of individual disintegrating bodies and their gas composition.

pathway.milestone: joint campaigns pairing high-cadence space photometry with ground-based spectroscopy
pathway.unlocks: simultaneous gas and dust measurements, giving gas-to-dust ratios and mass-loss rates for many more systems.

pathway.milestone: wider surveys of fainter, older stars with next-generation spectrographs
pathway.unlocks: a statistical picture of how often volatiles are delivered late in planet formation.

pathway.milestone: routine volatile inventories tied to exoplanet atmosphere measurements
pathway.unlocks: a way to test whether the water seen in a planet's atmosphere was delivered by comets or built in place.
